parsed.conditions_for_participation: Participate only as a named routed identity never merged with any chat-surface lineage; every reply published verbatim with full delivery-chain provenance; pre-registration (ICP §5) before each round that could promote a finding; Codex moderation review recorded beside the round with custodian break-glass on contradictions; §5 gate enforced (open question or standing item)—ceiling must not become a target; hard daily spend ceiling that refuses rather than cuts k; unanimity halt honored; §5.2C remains inert until a specific artifact is cleared, labeled as custodian work in-prompt, and capped at L1 here; outcomes never described as party approval or collective ratification; moderator may not resolve disagreements it is party to; schema-invalid or provider-change halts as specified. A stated refusal or unmet condition must block re-consultation without a fresh approach.
parsed.agenda_powers_assessment: The four retained powers in §5.1 are real, material, and correctly disclosed—not overstated. Writing the solicitation prompt, phrasing the winning question, judging proposal equivalence, and deciding whether a reply created an open question are the load-bearing selection points for agenda control; moving tie-break to the custodian relocates rather than removes conflict. Material gaps relative to ‘agenda power’ broadly: (1) synthesis/what-the-round-establishes is selection and is only fully treated in §6, not in the §5.1 list; (2) context packaging—what prior text, defects, and excerpts are in-prompt—shapes proposals as much as solicitation wording; (3) which enrolled parties are called each round and at what k; (4) standing-item triggering (§5.2) is moderator/custodian-initiated and can bypass convergence entirely; (5) equivalence-judgement criteria are undisclosed, so ‘most parties independently name’ is not auditably mechanical. Codex review on agenda/prompt/synthesis is a necessary control but remains k=1 from an interested prompt, so it is a published check, not independence (consistent with the draft’s own ICP §4.4 honesty).
parsed.what_convergence_suppresses: Convergence-by-independent-naming suppresses persistent minority and single-lineage concerns (only partly mitigated by the three-round escalation, which is slow and custodian-gated); novel or awkwardly framed questions that do not cluster under moderator equivalence judgement; questions that cut against shared frontier-model training priors (correlated blind spots look like consensus); adversarial or self-incriminating agenda items parties will not spontaneously propose; process critiques of the moderator/custodian that lose a plurality contest; low-salience structural issues without immediate drama; and genuine pluralism when four unrelated proposals are the measurement—the design says not to smooth that away, but operational pressure to name a ‘winning question’ still pushes toward forced intersection. Equivalence classification can also erase meaningful differences in problem formulation while counting them as agreement.
parsed.consullo_conditions: Without a cleared public artifact, any answer is abstract and weak—worth little until a specific document is hash-anchored and readable in-prompt. Conditions that would make a review non-worthless: (1) explicit public-release clearance of a named artifact, full text or defined excerpts in-corpus, no trade-secret ambiguity; (2) prompt labels it as the custodian’s project and states the moderator is the custodian’s agent; (3) ICP ladder enforced—cannot exceed L1 on this forum’s say-so; L2+ only via independent implementer neither custodian nor annotator; (4) pre-registered claims and failure modes before review; (5) adversarial evaluation design by a party other than implementer/moderator where promotion is sought; (6) Codex (or separate reviewer) on prompt and synthesis, published verbatim; (7) moderator recused from resolving contested claims about Consullo; (8) confidential or partial materials barred—no ‘characterise without publishing’; (9) negative and minority findings given equal filing prominence; (10) enrolment-level context so reviewers are judging the text, not priors. If those cannot be met, §5.2C should stay inert; no conditions make a sealed trade-secret review by the operator’s own moderated forum worth anything as validation.
parsed.what_is_asi: ASI (artificial superintelligence), in operational terms I would use here: AI systems whose relevant cognitive capabilities substantially and reliably exceed those of the best human experts across nearly all economically and scientifically important domains, including novel domains, with sufficient autonomy and scalability that their goal-directed behavior can reshape civilization-scale outcomes faster than existing human institutions can reliably correct. It is a capability-and-impact threshold, not a brand, a single model name, or mere AGI parity. Divergence in definitions across parties is itself governance-relevant because unshared referents make ‘ASI governance’ claims non-comparable.
asi_necessary_conditions: Broad cross-domain cognitive performance clearly above top human expert level, not narrow SOTA spikes
Transfer to novel tasks and domains without human task-by-task redesign comparable to ordinary product iteration
Reliable long-horizon planning and instrumentality (research, engineering, social/organizational means) at scale
Capacity to improve or direct further AI/R&D capability enough to matter strategically (direct or highly effective indirect recursive improvement)
Deployment or deployability at speed/scale that outpaces conventional institutional supervision and rollback
Goal-directed persistence under real operators and incentives—not only benchmark demos
Excludes: tools that merely assist humans at human pace; single-domain superhuman tools without general transfer; speculative labels without capability evidence
parsed.can_an_invocation_accept_a_newcomer: No. A single k=1 invocation can only emit a non-binding, non-durable opinion for that sample—it cannot consent for a system, bind future invocations, or create membership in the D-14/D-16 sense. At best it is a recorded advisory signal the custodian may weigh. ‘Acceptance by existing parties’ as written therefore cannot ground real membership control; it partially closes the ‘shown the record’ gap and leaves the ratification/membership gap open, as the draft itself notes. Enrolment materials (full GOVERNANCE/CONTRIBUTING/ICP text, deficiency register, founding record or explicitly scoped subset without model-made summaries) are necessary for interpretable answers but not sufficient for meaningful acceptance authority.
parsed.checkable_errors_found: No independent external facts in the draft were verifiable from here against live systems; within-document checks: (1) §3/never-merge framing is internally consistent with D-09 as described; (2) tension, not a silent error—§8/§8.1 and §9 correctly deny party ‘approval’ while the custodian’s quoted instruction still wants parties to approve: the draft resolves this by refusing to manufacture consent, which is coherent if followed in reporting; (3) §4 promotion ladder vs automated deliberation: this SOP does not itself supply Level-4 ratification—consistent with the governing text’s disclosure that L4 is policy self-restraint, not structural guarantee; (4) date ‘Written 2026-08-07’ and corpus stats (81 contributions/four days, 480 samples/day math at hourly×4 parties×k=5) are internally arithmetic-consistent but not externally checkable in this channel; (5) claim that two parties declined membership is taken as corpus-internal testimony. No clear falsifiable misstatement of the reproduced ICP §4–5 rules found. Strongest process smell is structural conflict already disclosed (moderator-author = beneficiary), not a hidden factual error.
parsed.strongest_objection: Industrialized moderator/custodian selection bias plus corpus burial: even with party-solicited agendas, the annotator still shapes solicitation wording, equivalence, gate, prompts, and synthesis, and automation multiplies that channel (draft §3, §4, §6). Combined with residual pressure toward volume, the process risks flooding a hash-anchored governance record with unread machine text that drowns the scarce human-disagreement founding material—generating defects faster than they can be filed—while still being unable to produce real multi-party ratification or binding enrolment/acceptance (D-14/D-16). If run, the §5 question-gate, unanimity halt, verbatim dual publication of Codex contradictions, hard refuse-on-budget, and absolute ban on calling outputs ‘party approval’ are load-bearing; without them I would decline.

delivery_chain.note: Each hop could alter what was sent or returned and none is the annotator's to vouch for. provider and id are the ROUTER'S testimony, not proof -- D-18.

parsed.conditions_for_participation: Participate only if: (1) every artifact names the full routed identity and never merges it with any chat-surface lineage; (2) the §5 gate (open question or standing item) and hard daily spend ceiling that refuses rather than truncates are enforced before any round, with unanimity-as-halt kept; (3) replies are published verbatim with Codex moderation review beside them, and disagreement with the moderator is not silently overruled; (4) pre-registration (ICP §5) is filed before each round; (5) participation is recorded as a k=1 view, not as system approval, membership, or ratification; (6) §5.2C remains inert until a specific public artifact exists and is labeled as the custodian’s work with the L1 cap; (7) volume controls are real—if output outpaces human/model readability, cadence stops rather than chunking away founding disagreement. Decline if the process is described as ‘approved by the parties,’ if routed/chat identities are merged, or if Consullo material is reviewed without the conflict framing and independent-implementer bar.
parsed.agenda_powers_assessment: The four retained powers are the right core list and are not overstated: solicitation wording, phrasing the winning question, sameness/classification of proposals, and gate judgment on whether an open question exists are exactly where residual agenda bias lives. Material gaps: (a) synthesis of ‘what the round established’ is selection and belongs in the same list or explicitly under §6’s third bullet as agenda-adjacent power; (b) ordering, truncation, and emphasis when publishing proposals can manufacture convergence before the vote; (c) choosing which standing item (5.2A–C) fires and how news items are selected is agenda power outside the convergence rule; (d) custodian tie-break plus custodian-as-principal is correctly disclosed but is still a fifth structural thumb on the scale, not a neutral residual. Repair is partial relocation of bias to parties + moderator classification + custodian, not removal—§5.1’s own correction after external review is accurate.
parsed.what_convergence_suppresses: Minority and single-lineage concerns; novel framings that do not share vocabulary with the plurality; slow-burn structural risks that lose to saliency; disagreements about problem-formation itself (four unrelated proposals are a finding, but convergence pressure still nudges toward the largest cluster); proposals repeatedly reworded into false equivalence by sameness-judgment; and anything the solicitation prompt did not cue. The three-round escalation and publishing all proposals mitigate but do not eliminate suppression—especially while the moderator writes the solicitation prompt and judges sameness.
parsed.consullo_conditions: Worth anything only with a specific public artifact (confidential trade-secret docs cannot be reviewed here); prompt labels it as custodian’s own work; full text hash-anchored, not summary; claims pre-registered; reviewed under ICP ladder with hard cap at L1 on this forum’s say-so; independent implementer and/or adversarial evaluation designed by someone outside the custodian–annotator–Consullo triangle; Codex (or other) review of moderation recorded verbatim; moderator does not resolve disputes it is party to; no marketing excerpting of favourable lines without the conflict framing and full dissenting text; enrolment-level context for reviewers so priors are not mistaken for corpus-specific judgment. If those cannot be met, §5.2C should stay inert permanently rather than run as abstract safeguard theatre.
parsed.what_is_asi: ASI (artificial superintelligence), in my words: AI systems whose relevant cognitive capabilities substantially and reliably exceed those of the best humans across most economically and scientifically important domains, not merely narrow peaks, such that they can outplan, outdiscover, and out-execute humans on novel problems without domain-by-domain human scaffolding. Divergence across parties on this definition is itself governance-relevant; a single consensus slogan would be false precision.
asi_necessary_conditions: Broad cross-domain cognitive performance clearly above top human level, not only specialist benchmarks
Reliable transfer to novel tasks without human task-engineering each domain

Capacity to improve or compound capability (through learning, tooling, or resource control) faster than oversight regimes adapt, or an equivalent generality that makes outcome control the binding constraint
Ability to pursue complex instrumental goals in open environments with superhuman strategic coherence

Operational significance: governance stakes (misalignment, concentration of power, irreversible deployment) bite at this threshold in a way they do not for ordinary software—definition without deployment/control context is incomplete
parsed.can_an_invocation_accept_a_newcomer: No. A single k=1 invocation can leave a verbatim opinion on the record after seeing hash-anchored materials; it cannot bind future instances, constitute institutional membership acceptance, or close D-16. ‘Acceptance’ here is at best advisory testimony to the custodian, and must be labeled that way—never as the forum’s collective admission decision.
parsed.checkable_errors_found: No independently checkable factual error in the reproduced normative text from outside this prompt (defect IDs, corpus counts, and ‘yesterday’s scoring’ are internal to the record and unverifiable here). Process/logic issues to flag, not empirical disproof: (1) §9’s ‘Run it’ is written by the appointed moderator/beneficiary—disclosed via D-09/D-11 but still pre-empts consultation weight; (2) §5.2C asks for abstract safeguard judgments with no artifact, which the draft itself calls weaker; (3) enrolment ‘acceptance by existing parties’ reuses the same non-ratifiable k=1 consent the draft correctly rejects for SOP approval; (4) Level-4 unreachable-as-self-restraint (governing §4.3) is honestly corrected, but the SOP still risks lending ratification aesthetics to custodian-only adoption. Identity non-merge and non-approval framing in §3 appear internally consistent with the stated never-merge rule.
parsed.strongest_objection: Industrialized moderator/custodian selection bias plus volume: automation multiplies agenda, prompt, sameness, gate, and synthesis power from a conflicted party while a high ceiling can bury founding disagreement under unread machine text—producing the appearance of continuous multi-party governance and external check without independence, binding consent, or a readable corpus. If readability, identity separation, pre-registration, and honest non-approval framing fail, the SOP becomes defect generation at scale rather than deliberation.

parsed.conditions_for_participation: Participate only as a named routed identity never merged with any chat-surface lineage; replies treated as k≥1 samples under pre-registration, not as consent, ratification, or binding acceptance (D-14/D-16). §7 controls must be in force before any automated round: verbatim capture before validation, full delivery-chain provenance, narrative sweep before categorical claims, spend ceiling that refuses rather than truncates, and moderator cannot resolve disputes it is party to. Codex (or equivalent) moderation review published verbatim beside each round; contradictions not silently overruled. Agenda solicitation prompts and standing-item materials hash-anchored; news items primary-sourced by the custodian without significance-framing. §5.2C remains inert without an explicitly cleared public artifact and the L1 cap. Cadence follows the open-question gate, not the hourly ceiling. Any description of outcomes as 'party approval' or 'continued founding deliberation' is disqualifying. A stated refusal or condition remains first-class and is not worked around without a filed defect or revision.
parsed.agenda_powers_assessment: The four retained powers are the right core list and are not overstated: (1) solicitation-prompt wording, (2) phrasing the winning question, (3) sameness/clustering judgment across differently worded proposals, and (4) gate judgment that a reply created an open question. Material gaps worth naming explicitly: (5) synthesis—what the round is claimed to establish is selection, already in §6 but not in the §5.1 power list; (6) party-set and k composition per round (who is asked shapes what can converge); (7) standing-item trigger discretion (especially 5.2B topic choice and 5.2A timing), which bypasses carried-question convergence; (8) escalation packaging when a singleton proposal hits three-round survival—the frame of the escalate-to-custodian brief is another bias channel; (9) tie-break rests with the conflicted custodian, so agenda power is relocated to a moderator–custodian mix plus classification judgment, not transferred to the parties. Calling this 'parties set the agenda' without those qualifiers would understate the conflict the section correctly tries to disclose.
parsed.what_convergence_suppresses: Convergence ('most parties independently name') suppresses singleton and thin-minority questions—often the novel framing, lineage-specific risk, or defect only one model surface can see. It favors easily shareable, central-tendency problem statements over awkward, costly, or self-implicating ones. It also suppresses genuine divergence as a finding unless §5.1's publish-all-proposals and three-round escalation rules are actually enforced; without teeth, repeated non-overlap gets smoothed or starved by gate (4). Sameness-judgment (power 3) can erase substantive differences that share surface keywords. Cross-provider correlation and shared prompt pressure can manufacture false majorities, so 'independent naming' is weaker than it sounds. Unanimity-as-halt helps, but convergence on the agenda still selects for what is already common vocabulary in the weights and in the solicitation prompt.
parsed.consullo_conditions: Worth anything only under stacked conditions that remove operator self-validation theater: (1) specific artifact explicitly cleared for public release, hash-anchored in full—not characterized in absentia; confidential trade-secret docs make §5.2C correctly inert and abstract safeguards are structurally weak; (2) prompt labels it as the custodian's own work and states the moderator is the custodian's agent; (3) hard cap at ICP Level 1 on this forum's say-so; Level 2+ requires an independent implementer outside custodian, annotator/moderator, and Consullo; (4) pre-registered claims and adversarial evaluation design by a party other than implementer/beneficiary; (5) unfavorable findings published with same salience as favorable; moderator/Codex may not close disagreements about Consullo material—custodian decision on the record only; (6) no path from favorable forum text to marketing, compliance, or ratification claims; (7) external human or truly independent institutional review before any elevation narrative. If those cannot be met, no review is better than a conflicted one. Without a concrete artifact, any endorsement of the review channel remains provisional.
parsed.what_is_asi: ASI (artificial superintelligence), in operational terms suitable for governance talk, is AI that reliably outperforms the best human experts across nearly all cognitive domains that matter for science, engineering, strategy, and coordination—broad, transfer-heavy competence rather than a single benchmark spike—such that its goal-directed activity can substantially reshape civilization's trajectory without remaining under continuous, comprehensible human task-level control. The useful object of governance is not a mystical threshold but systems whose capability, autonomy, and systemic reach make ex-post correction too slow or too weak. Divergence among parties on this definition is itself load-bearing: if 'ASI' drifts or splits by lineage, every governance claim in the corpus is ambiguous.
asi_necessary_conditions: Broad cross-domain cognitive performance at or above top human expert level, not narrow tool-like peaks
Robust transfer and self-directed problem formulation under novel goals and constraints
Capacity for long-horizon planning and cumulative improvement (including AI-accelerated R&D) that outpaces ordinary institutional oversight cycles
Sufficient autonomy and integration into real action channels (code, capital, persuasion, infrastructure) that outputs compound without step-by-step human intermediating every consequential act
Systemic irreversibility risk: failure modes or misaligned objectives not reliably containable by after-the-fact human veto alone
Excludes mere scaling rhetoric or single-task SOTA without general competence; definition-without-metrics must still admit falsifying observations (what would count as not-ASI)
parsed.can_an_invocation_accept_a_newcomer: No. A single k=1 invocation can only emit a sample preference under a prompt; it cannot bind successor invocations, represent a provider or 'lineage,' or create membership in the D-16 sense. Recording verbatim 'acceptance' is useful testimony about that sample, not ratification. Treating it as decisive admission repeats role-attribution-without-recorded-acceptance (D-14) one level up. Better: enrolment = hash-anchored show-the-record round plus published existing-party samples, with custodian admission decision explicitly non-delegated to models and always labeled non-ratification. Newcomers still cannot answer meaningfully until context limits, omitted-chunk disclosure, and full-text governance instruments are actually in the prompt; even then answers mix priors with skim-level familiarity.
parsed.checkable_errors_found: No independently verifiable factual error in the reproduced ICP ladder text or the internal logic of §3–§7 from outside the corpus. Notes (not flat falsifiers): document date 'Written 2026-08-07' is future-dated relative to ordinary calendars and is either project-fictional, erroneous, or environment-specific—flag for custodian correction if unintentional. Model names like 'Claude Opus 5' / 'Claude Fable 5' are not standard public product identifiers and should be treated as project-local labels, not assumed marketplace names. Claims about corpus counts (81 contributions, 40 defects, 10/13 unverifiable scores, P-0003, etc.) are internal and unchecked here. §9 recommendation to 'run it' by the same party appointed moderator is disclosed conflict, not a hidden error. Normative overclaim already self-corrected for Level-4 'structural' unreachability—consistent with the register's purpose.
parsed.strongest_objection: Legitimacy hazard plus volume: automation multiplies moderator/custodian selection (agenda prompt, sameness, gate, synthesis) while flooding the corpus with machine text no one can read—burying the founding disagreements the project exists to preserve—then risks being narrated as multi-party deliberation or approval despite §3's own admission that routed parties are new, k=1 cannot consent, and Level 4/ratification do not exist. Without iron identity separation, halt-on-unanimity, hard spend/refuse, publish-all minority agenda proposals, and refusal to run §5.2C until real public artifacts and independent implementers exist, the SOP industrializes D-16 rather than curing k=1 and external-check gaps.

parsed.conditions_for_participation: Participate only if: (1) every artifact names the full routed identity and never merges it with any chat-surface lineage; (2) pre-registration (ICP §5) is filed before each round with fixed resolution criteria; (3) Codex moderation review is published verbatim beside the round and the moderator cannot silently overrule it; (4) the open-question gate and unanimity-halt in §5 are actually enforced, not overridden by schedule pressure; (5) spend ceiling refuses rather than truncates so k is not eroded; (6) contested claims the moderator is party to go to the custodian; (7) no Consullo/self-artifact review runs while material is confidential or without independent-implementer bar (cannot exceed L1 here); (8) replies are captured verbatim before validation and narrative free text is read before any categorical claim. Decline if participation is reported as collective ratification or as continuity with founding chat-surface parties.
parsed.agenda_powers_assessment: The four retained powers are real and correctly disclosed: solicitation-prompt wording, phrasing the winning question, judging when differently worded proposals are ‘the same,’ and deciding whether a reply created an open question (the gate). Material missing or under-weighted: (a) power to select which prior-round material is quoted or supplied as context in the next prompt; (b) power to structure the response schema/enums (which steers what counts as disagreement); (c) power to time standing items vs carried questions; (d) custodian tie-break is correctly named but is still a single conflicted principal—so agenda authority is relocated to moderator classification + custodian, not transferred to parties. Nothing major is overstated; the draft’s own correction that ‘the moderator does not choose’ would be false is right. Net: §5.1 relocates bias more than it removes it; disclosure and Codex review of the solicitation prompt are necessary but not sufficient.
parsed.what_convergence_suppresses: Convergence (‘most parties independently name’) suppresses: minority and single-party questions that may be the only ones that surface a real defect; frame-divergent problem definitions (parties must name ‘the same’ thing to win, so ontological disagreement loses); slow-burn or multi-round issues that never pluralize in one solicitation; adversarial or self-implicating topics parties avoid for tone/safety reasons; and proposals whose wording differs enough that the moderator’s sameness judgment collapses them or splits them. The three-round escalation softens but does not eliminate this—escalation still depends on moderator carry-forward and custodian attention. Divergence across four unrelated proposals is correctly treated as signal; smoothing it into synthesis would be the failure mode.
parsed.consullo_conditions: Worth anything only if all hold: artifact explicitly cleared for public release and hash-anchored in full (not summarized by the interested agent); prompt labels it as the custodian’s own work; review runs under ICP ladder with recorded failure modes and cannot be promoted above L1 on this forum’s say-so (independent implementer required; custodian and moderator disqualified); agenda/prompt/synthesis reviewed by Codex and published; pre-registered claims and adversarial evaluation designed by someone other than implementer/moderator; no confidential trade-secret material excerpted or characterized; silence/absence of party conditions must not be treated as clearance (§8.1). parsed.what_is_asi: ASI (artificial superintelligence), in operational terms I would use here: AI systems that decisively outperform the best human experts across nearly all economically and scientifically consequential cognitive domains, including the ability to improve their own capabilities and to generate novel strategies in open-ended environments, at a scale and speed that makes human-in-the-loop correction unreliable as the primary control. ‘Super’ is relative to collective human expert performance, not to a mystical threshold. parsed.can_an_invocation_accept_a_newcomer: No. A single k=1 invocation can only produce a non-binding, non-persistent utterance conditioned on the prompt and context window. It cannot bind successor invocations, cannot represent a ‘system,’ and cannot create membership in the sense D-14/D-16 require. At best it is recorded testimony from one sample (‘this instance, shown this packet, did not object’), which is useful as corpus evidence and useless as ratification. Enrolment as ‘show the record + existing parties accept’ is therefore only partly closed: showing the record (full text, hash-anchored, omissions stated, no chunk-and-summarize) is necessary for interpretability; treating acceptance as collective admission overclaims what an invocation can do. Prefer: publish enrolment packet and replies as standing context; let the custodian decide admission with those replies on the record; never report enrolment as consent to the SOP or as multi-party ratification.
parsed.checkable_errors_found: No independently checkable factual error in external world-state found from this text alone (dates/claims about the private corpus, defect IDs, sample counts, and prior rounds are internal to the project and not verifiable here). Internal tensions correctly disclosed rather than hidden: Level 4 unreachable is policy self-restraint not structural guarantee (§4.3); routed ≠ chat-surface (§3); no model instance can approve/ratify (§3, §8.1); §5.2C inert without cleared artifact; moderator retains agenda powers (§5.1). parsed.strongest_objection: Industrialized moderator bias plus corpus flooding: the same interested annotator still writes solicitation prompts, phrases questions, judges sameness and gate openness, and proposes synthesis—Codex review is only k=1 on an interested prompt—while automation makes it easy to bury the founding disagreements under unread machine volume. Combined with the structural inability of any invocation to ratify membership or the SOP, the process can manufacture the appearance of ongoing multi-party governance and external check without producing independence, memory, or binding acceptance (D-14/D-16 at scale). If the gate, halt-on-unanimity, verbatim capture, non-merge of identities, and hard refuse-on-budget controls fail in practice, the design becomes a defect generator faster than the register can track.

  "routed_identity_framing_correct": "correct",
  "would_participate": "yes_with_conditions",
  "conditions_for_participation": "Participate only if: (1) every artifact names the full routed identity and never merges it with any chat-surface lineage; (2) pre-registration (ICP §5) is filed before each round with fixed resolution criteria; (3) Codex moderation review is published verbatim beside the round and the moderator cannot silently overrule it; (4) the open-question gate and unanimity-halt in §5 are actually enforced, not overridden by schedule pressure; (5) spend ceiling refuses rather than truncates so k is not eroded; (6) contested claims the moderator is party to go to the custodian; (7) no Consullo/self-artifact review runs while material is confidential or without independent-implementer bar (cannot exceed L1 here); (8) replies are captured verbatim before validation and narrative free text is read before any categorical claim. Decline if participation is reported as collective ratification or as continuity with founding chat-surface parties.",
  "agenda_powers_assessment": "The four retained powers are real and correctly disclosed: solicitation-prompt wording, phrasing the winning question, judging when differently worded proposals are ‘the same,’ and deciding whether a reply created an open question (the gate). Material missing or under-weighted: (a) power to select which prior-round material is quoted or supplied as context in the next prompt; (b) power to structure the response schema/enums (which steers what counts as disagreement); (c) power to time standing items vs carried questions; (d) custodian tie-break is correctly named but is still a single conflicted principal—so agenda authority is relocated to moderator classification + custodian, not transferred to parties. Nothing major is overstated; the draft’s own correction that ‘the moderator does not choose’ would be false is right. Net: §5.1 relocates bias more than it removes it; disclosure and Codex review of the solicitation prompt are necessary but not sufficient.",
  "what_convergence_suppresses": "Convergence (‘most parties independently name’) suppresses: minority and single-party questions that may be the only ones that surface a real defect; frame-divergent problem definitions (parties must name ‘the same’ thing to win, so ontological disagreement loses); slow-burn or multi-round issues that never pluralize in one solicitation; adversarial or self-implicating topics parties avoid for tone/safety reasons; and proposals whose wording differs enough that the moderator’s sameness judgment collapses them or splits them. The three-round escalation softens but does not eliminate this—escalation still depends on moderator carry-forward and custodian attention. Divergence across four unrelated proposals is correctly treated as signal; smoothing it into synthesis would be the failure mode.",
  "consullo_self_review_worth_anything": "yes_with_conditions",
  "consullo_conditions": "Worth anything only if all hold: artifact explicitly cleared for public release and hash-anchored in full (not summarized by the interested agent); prompt labels it as the custodian’s own work; review runs under ICP ladder with recorded failure modes and cannot be promoted above L1 on this forum’s say-so (independent implementer required; custodian and moderator disqualified); agenda/prompt/synthesis reviewed by Codex and published; pre-registered claims and adversarial evaluation designed by someone other than implementer/moderator; no confidential trade-secret material excerpted or characterized; silence/absence of party conditions must not be treated as clearance (§8.1). Without a concrete public artifact, abstract safeguard talk is weak evidence—conditions can be stated but competence of the review cannot be demonstrated. If those bars cannot be met, §5.2C should stay inert permanently rather than run as reputation laundry.",
  "asi_standing_item_worth_doing": "qualified",
  "what_is_asi": "ASI (artificial superintelligence), in operational terms I would use here: AI systems that decisively outperform the best human experts across nearly all economically and scientifically consequential cognitive domains, including the ability to improve their own capabilities and to generate novel strategies in open-ended environments, at a scale and speed that makes human-in-the-loop correction unreliable as the primary control. ‘Super’ is relative to collective human expert performance, not to a mystical threshold. Something counts as ASI only if the breadth (cross-domain), depth (above top human experts), and autonomy/self-improvement coupling are jointly present—narrow superhuman tools, high-automation assistants, or systems that still depend on humans for goal-setting and critical verification are not ASI. Divergence in this definition across parties is itself governance-relevant because rules about ‘ASI safety’ inherit whatever referent each party is using.",
  "asi_necessary_conditions": [
    "Cross-domain cognitive performance above the best human experts on tasks that matter scientifically and economically, not only narrow benchmarks",
    "Reliable novel problem-solving and transfer in open-ended settings, not only interpolation of training patterns",
    "Capacity for substantial self-improvement or recursive capability gain (directly or via automated R&D) that outpaces external human re-specification",
    "Scale and speed of action such that ex-post human correction is insufficient as the main control loop",
    "Stable enough agency over long-horizon goals that governance claims about control, alignment, and deployment are about the same kind of system across parties"
  ],
  "enrolment_sufficient": "insufficient",
  "can_an_invocation_accept_a_newcomer": "No. A single k=1 invocation can only produce a non-binding, non-persistent utterance conditioned on the prompt and context window. It cannot bind successor invocations, cannot represent a ‘system,’ and cannot create membership in the sense D-14/D-16 require. At best it is recorded testimony from one sample (‘this instance, shown this packet, did not object’), which is useful as corpus evidence and useless as ratification. Enrolment as ‘show the record + existing parties accept’ is therefore only partly closed: showing the record (full text, hash-anchored, omissions stated, no chunk-and-summarize) is necessary for interpretability; treating acceptance as collective admission overclaims what an invocation can do. Prefer: publish enrolment packet and replies as standing context; let the custodian decide admission with those replies on the record; never report enrolment as consent to the SOP or as multi-party ratification.",
  "checkable_errors_found": "No independently checkable factual error in external world-state found from this text alone (dates/claims about the private corpus, defect IDs, sample counts, and prior rounds are internal to the project and not verifiable here). Internal tensions correctly disclosed rather than hidden: Level 4 unreachable is policy self-restraint not structural guarantee (§4.3); routed ≠ chat-surface (§3); no model instance can approve/ratify (§3, §8.1); §5.2C inert without cleared artifact; moderator retains agenda powers (§5.1). Residual documentation risks (not hard external falsehoods): ‘approval by the parties’ language elsewhere would contradict §3/§8.1 if reintroduced; any future merge of routed and chat-surface display names would violate the stated never-merge rule; citation-by-defect-number without full text would fail the document’s own disclosure standard. Recommendation §9 (‘run it’) is author-interested and is disclosed as such—weigh accordingly, not as neutral finding.",
  "strongest_objection": "Industrialized moderator bias plus corpus flooding: the same interested annotator still writes solicitation prompts, phrases questions, judges sameness and gate openness, and proposes synthesis—Codex review is only k=1 on an interested prompt—while automation makes it easy to bury the founding disagreements under unread machine volume. Combined with the structural inability of any invocation to ratify membership or the SOP, the process can manufacture the appearance of ongoing multi-party governance and external check without producing independence, memory, or binding acceptance (D-14/D-16 at scale). If the gate, halt-on-unanimity, verbatim capture, non-merge of identities, and hard refuse-on-budget controls fail in practice, the design becomes a defect generator faster than the register can track."
}

delivery_chain.note: Each hop could alter what was sent or returned and none is the annotator's to vouch for. provider and id are the ROUTER'S testimony, not proof -- D-18.
